messages:
oliver: Heads-up: several onboarding/sample-apps hit a build error with Next middleware after pulling the latest SDK. Build fails with "Could not resolve 'fs'" and vite/next resolving the CJS entrypoint.

priya: I saw that too. repro is simple: importing at module scope in middleware -> bundler pulls require() path which references node-only helpers.

oliver: error snippet:
```
Failed to compile.
Module not found: Can't resolve 'fs' in 'node_modules/@redwood/inference/lib'
```

antoine: root cause: package.json currently points consumers to a generic main/import that still re-exports node-specific code. ESM bundlers sometimes prefer import -> ends up hitting the CJS layer because of missing explicit exports for edge targets.

claire: short-term workaround for affected apps: dynamic import inside middleware handler and load the edge-tailored build:```js
export default async function middleware(req) {
  const sdk = await import('@redwood/inference/edge');
  const client = new sdk.Client({ auth: { mode: 'edge' } });
  // handle request
}
```
This avoids bundlers resolving node-only bits at build time.

antoine: long-term fix: add an explicit export path for edge in package.json so bundlers can pick the right file automatically. e.g. ```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "edge": "./dist/edge/index.js"
  },
  "./edge": "./dist/edge/index.js"
}
```
That lets `import '@redwood/inference'` still work in node but bundlers that support conditional exports (like Next/Vite) can choose the edge entrypoint.

priya: +1. also adding a dedicated entry path `@redwood/inference/edge` is helpful for older bundlers that don't honor exports conditions.

claire: typing problems: TS still complains when projects target dom/edge because SDK typings reference NodeJS.Timer and Buffer. Proposed solution: ship a separate types file for edge that uses DOM timer typings and avoids Node globals. add an exports mapping to types too so consumers get the correct d.ts.

antoine: I'm working on a small edge shim that strips timers and fs usage at bundle-time and exposes minimal runtime helpers (no setTimeout at module init). will open PR with unit tests that run under a service-worker-like test harness.

ci-bot: CI: draft PR created (sdk#420) -> includes exports.edge + edge build + edge-types. running matrix job 1123.

oliver: will test the draft in our sample-apps once CI finishes. if green we can cut an rc and update the examples to demonstrate `import '@redwood/inference/edge'` and middleware usage.

priya: docs-bot: please add a note in SDK migration guide: "If you use Next middleware or other edge runtimes, prefer the edge entrypoint or upgrade to SDK >=0.11.x that includes conditional exports."

docs-bot: noted. created docs PR: docs/sdk-edge-entry.md and linked to examples repo.

claire: followups: 1) publish rc with edge export, 2) add CI job that bundles SDK with next/vite to catch regressions, 3) update sample-apps and onboarding quickstart.

antoine: will also add a small lint rule to prevent accidental top-level background timers in future changes.

oliver: thanks all. this should cut the friction for customers using Next Edge middleware. will report back after we test the rc in staging.
